name: @projexlight/sdk-rebac
summary: Relationship-based access control (ReBAC) for ProjexCloud: model 'who is related to what and how' (Zanzibar-style relation tuples), then ask 'can this user perform this action on this resource?' Universal authorization primitive — every other SDK delegates 'is this allowed' to this one so policy logic stays centralized + auditable.

endpoints.description: Write a relationship tuple (subject, relation, object). Idempotent on the tuple key.
Update the scope (tenant_id / bu_id pin) of an existing relationship.
Decision endpoint — returns allow/deny + the relationship chain that justified it.

events.name: rebac.relationship.added.v1
events.description: Tuple committed; carries (subject, relation, object) keys.

events.name: rebac.relationship.removed.v1
events.description: Tuple removed (explicit revoke or cascade from upstream change).

events.name: rebac.decision.evaluated.v1
events.description: Authorization check evaluated; carries decision + walked-edges trace.

models.description: Tuple row: (subject_kind, subject_id, relation, object_kind, object_id, tenant_id, bu_id). Index for both directions.
Per-check audit row: principal, action, resource, decision (allow/deny), walked_edges, evaluated_at.

hooks.name: addRelationship
hooks.description: Write a tuple — idempotent on (subject, relation, object). Emits .added.v1.

hooks.name: removeRelationship
hooks.description: Remove a tuple. Cascades dependent permissions if cascade flag set.

hooks.name: checkPermission
hooks.description: Universal authorization check; walks the tuple graph to a fixed depth + returns allow/deny + edge trace.

hooks.name: expandPermissions
hooks.description: List every (subject, action) the given principal can perform on the given resource. Useful for tenant-admin UIs that show 'who can do what'.

scenarios.title: Make a user the owner of a tenant org
scenarios.when_to_use: Onboarding — first admin of a new tenant gets the 'owner' relation, which other SDKs trust as the highest-permission anchor.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Tuple persisted; emits .added.v1. Subsequent checkPermission calls for that persona on org-scoped actions resolve allow.

scenarios.title: Can this user edit this document?
scenarios.when_to_use: Per-request authorization in any SDK that operates on resources. The check walks the relation graph (persona → team_member → team → editor → document).
scenarios.expected_outcome: Decision row written + emitted. allow=true with walked_edges showing the path. Default deny if no path found.

scenarios.title: Tenant admin UI: 'what can Alice do on this project?'
scenarios.when_to_use: Permissions-explorer panel — operator wants to see the full set of (action, resource) pairs Alice can perform without making N check calls.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Returns array of { action, allow, walked_edges } — UI renders as a permissions matrix.

scenarios.title: Reactive: remove all relationships when a persona offboards
scenarios.when_to_use: Persona leaves the company; cascade-remove every tuple they're the subject of so their old permissions don't persist.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Every tuple where the persona was subject removed; emits .removed.v1 per tuple. Future checkPermission for this persona returns deny.

scenarios.title: Scope a relationship to a single business unit
scenarios.when_to_use: Multi-BU tenant — grant 'editor' on a project only within BU-A, not the whole org. Required for the six-layer scope model.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Tuple bound to BU-A. checkPermission outside BU-A's scope returns deny even for the same project.

compliance_posture.notes: Every decision is auditable to the relation chain walked — full SOC2-CC6.1 + ISO 27001 access-control audit trail without needing separate access logs. Cascade-remove on persona offboard is the GDPR Art-32 + 'principle of least privilege' implementation lever.

pricing_skus.unit_description: per checkPermission call (cached decisions billed at lower rate)
